1.note: The word translated “overcome” (κατέλαβεν) can also be translated “comprehended.” It refers to getting a grip on an enemy to defeat him.
The phrase “only born” is from the Greek word “μονογενους”, which is sometimes translated “only begotten” or “one and only”.
The phrase “only born” is from the Greek word “μονογενη”, which is sometimes translated “only begotten” or “one and only”.
“Behold”, from “ἰδοὺ”, means look at, take notice, observe, see, or gaze at. It is often used as an interjection.

2.note: 2 to 3 metretes is about 20 to 30 U. S. Gallons, or 75 to 115 liters.

3.note: The word translated “anew” here and in John 3:7 (ἄνωθεν) also means “again” and “from above”.
The same Greek word (πνεῦμα) means wind, breath, and spirit.
The phrase “only born” is from the Greek word “μονογενη”, which is sometimes translated “only begotten” or “one and only”.
The same word can be translated “disobeys” or “disbelieves” in this context.

5.note: NU omits from “waiting” in verse 3 to the end of verse 4.

6.note: A denarius was a silver coin worth about a day’s wages for an agricultural laborer, so 200 denarii would be between 6 and 7 month’s pay.
25 to 30 stadia is about 5 to 6 kilometers or about 3 to 4 miles
Greek and Hebrew use the same word for “heaven”, “the heavens”, “the sky”, and “the air”.

8.note: NU includes John 7:53–John 8:11, but puts brackets around it to indicate that the textual critics had less confidence that this was original.

10.note: The “Feast of the Dedication” is the Greek name for “Hanukkah”, a celebration of the rededication of the Temple.

11.note: 15 stadia is about 2.8 kilometers or 1.7 miles
NU omits “from the place where the dead man was lying.”

12.note: a Roman pound of 12 ounces, or about 340 grams
300 denarii was about a year’s wages for an agricultural laborer.
“Hosanna” means “save us” or “help us, we pray”.

14.note: Greek παρακλητον: Counselor, Helper, Intercessor, Advocate, and Comforter.

15.note: Greek Parakletos: Counselor, Helper, Advocate, Intercessor, and Comforter.

19.note: “the sixth hour” would have been 6:00 a.m. according to the Roman timekeeping system, or noon for the Jewish timekeeping system in use, then.
100 Roman pounds of 12 ounces each, or about 72 pounds, or 33 Kilograms.

20.note: Rabboni is a transliteration of the Aramaic word for “great teacher.”

21.note: 200 cubits is about 100 yards or about 91 meters
The word for “brothers” here may be also correctly translated “brothers and sisters” or “siblings.”
